title: An independent TESS fit keeps the 2019-2026 WASP-167 b duration increase (5.6 min, 3.2-4.3 sigma); SuperWASP 2006-2008 data (T14 176 +- 5 min) cannot confirm or reject its linear extrapolation
abstract: Question: Do independent data confirm the TESS transit-duration increase of the retrograde hot Jupiter WASP-167 b, which an earlier campaign study (sci:sha256:3f0985f4...) proposed as nodal precession? Method: We re-fit the five TESS 2-min sectors (2019-2026) with new code, six model variants and errors that we did not scale down. We measured the first pre-TESS duration from 23 partial transits in the public SuperWASP DR1 data (2006-2008). We fixed a/R* and Rp/R* to the TESS values and let the impact parameter, dilution and per-window baselines change. Injection-recovery at 24 other orbital phases gave the errors. Results: TESS T14 increases monotonically from 176.6 +- 1.2 min (2019.3) to 182.1 +- 0.9 min (2026.2), 0.69 +- 0.19 min/yr. A constant duration has p = 1.4e-5 to 1.4e-3 over the variants (3.2 to 4.3 sigma, against 6.7 sigma in the earlier study, which scaled its errors by 0.645). The trend stays after removal of gamma Doradus modes, with a quadratic baseline, with free Rp/R* and with theoretical limb darkening. SuperWASP gives T14 = 175.8 +- 4.8 min at 2007.5 (raw flux: 173.1 +- 5.9 min). The linear TESS trend predicts 168.5-170.5 min. Over 42 variant combinations the SuperWASP value is 0.2-1.6 sigma above the prediction and 0.1-1.2 sigma below the 2019 TESS value, so it does not discriminate. It limits the mean 2007-2026 rate to below about 0.85 min/yr (2 sigma). A J2 precession model gives the measured |db/dt| = 0.0036 /yr with a Love number k2 of about 0.007 for an equator-on star; we did not test the sign. Limitations: SuperWASP DR1 has too few transits; a decisive anchor needs about three times more. The TESS model has no gravity darkening. SuperWASP DR1 folded and binned transit with the best-fit model, the TESS-trend prediction and the 2026 TESS duration. The models differ by about 1 ppt at ingress and egress, near the bin errors.
TESS transits for each season and their differences to 2019: later seasons have earlier ingress and later egress.
